I revised /Users/Muramkar/code/idea-to-shipped/content/lessons/03-skills.md against the 1.3.1 SKILL.md files, the Claude Code docs (skills, discover-plugins and commands pages, fetched on 2026-10-24) and the repo. - **Accuracy:** the router Scene now reads to-spec, to-tickets and retro before it recommends skipping them, and it ends with `/retro`. The Lesson now gives the right reason the router never runs anything. Setup's domain docs step now says it only records the layout and doesn't create GLOSSARY.md or docs/adr/. I also added the rule that a slash name later in your message only gives the agent permission to run a Skill.
- **Final test and Checkpoints:** spot-asked-agent is replaced by spot-chained-skills, a new id that tests the rule that user-invoked Skills can't be chained. I added a 10th question, predict-setup-files, so goal 3 ("say what it writes") is checked. scenario-lost now uses a codebase-upkeep case, so it no longer repeats the router-stops premise. tracker-choice became tracker-other, a new id that tests the Other/Linear route. There are now 5 Checkpoints and 10 Final test questions, with right answers spread b c a d b / c a d b b d c d a c.
- **Try it yourself:** it no longer uses a heredoc, which fails in PowerShell 5.1. The agent now writes the Skill file, then you restart Claude Code. The steps say what you see when the Skill loads, and the Esc/Yes/exit guidance comes before step 1.
- **Reader glosses:** spec, triage labels, glossary, ADR, single-context, /clear, commit, turn, model, Node.js and gh are now each explained where they first appear.
- **Site story:** rebuilt from repo facts only.
  - The setup output and the Agent skills block are in first commit 4f849b9, with .scratch/lesson-site/.

  - I cut the "user scope, never ran npx" claim: no commit, PR or file in the repo backs it.
- **Quotes:** I turned the March-video quote into a paraphrase, because no text source on this machine has the exact words. I cut the Reddit and multi-repo bullets to stay within the word budget.

quiz.where: Final test, sequence-new-repo, line 449: "You've just installed Claude Code and want to use Matt's Skills on a brand-new project."
quiz.problem: The keyed order starts with the shell plugin install. The Lesson itself says the official marketplace is added the first time you start Claude Code, and the docs confirm it isn't registered on a machine where no interactive session has run yet. A careful reader who takes "just installed" to mean "never started" can argue the right answer fails at its first step, and every option installs before starting.
quiz.evidence: Lesson line 129: "`claude-plugins-official`, is added for you the first time you start Claude Code". https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins, Install from your shell: "on a machine where no one has opened an interactive Claude Code session yet, the official marketplace isn't registered, so a script that installs from it runs `claude plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official` before the install." The Try it (line 260) avoids this by requiring Claude Code "installed and signed in".
quiz.fix: Change the prompt to: "Claude Code is installed and you've signed in once. You want to use Matt's Skills on a brand-new project. Which order is right?" Keep the options and feedback as they are.

quiz.where: Final test, spot-both-routes, lines 412-422: "Sam's `/` menu lists grill-me twice, and the same goes for every one of Matt's Skills. Spot the mistake."
quiz.problem: The prompt has no mistake to spot. It describes no action by Sam, only a symptom, so this is really a 'what caused this?' question. The prompt's own words, "every one of Matt's Skills", rule out distractors c (Built-in clash) and d (update kept the old copy); c's feedback even admits only a few names clash. The right answer just repeats the highlighted body line 139 ("Install both and every Skill appears twice") and Common mistakes line 332, so it tests recall, not transfer.
quiz.evidence: Other Lessons' spot- questions describe what the person did, e.g. 00-start-here.md:289 lists Ana's numbered steps, and 04-grilling.md:402 lists Priya's actions. Lesson lines 139 and 332 state the answer word for word.
quiz.fix:
Replace with:
```test spot-both-routes
Sam set up a new laptop: (1) ran `claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official`; (2) ran `npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills` for his whole computer, so he'd have files he could edit; (3) started Claude Code in his repo and typed `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`; (4) typed `/grill-with-docs` to start his first feature. Spot the mistake.
- [ ] Step 1, the plugin install
  > The plugin is a complete route on its own, and it updates itself.
- [x] Step 2, the npx install
  > Right. The two routes are alternatives. With both, every Skill appears twice in his `/` menu. Pick one.
- [ ] Step 3, running setup in the repo
  > Setup belongs here: once per repo, before the engineering Skills.
- [ ] Step 4, starting with `/grill-with-docs`
  > In a repo, `/grill-with-docs` is the head of the Main flow.
```

quiz.where: Final test, predict-setup-files, lines 472-482: "A friend clones a repo where you ran `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` and committed the result... Where does her agent learn that tickets go under `.scratch/`?"

Under the 1.3.1 Skill, to-tickets learns the tracker from the provided config or tells you to run setup: ~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.3.1/skills/engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.md:11 "The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`."
quiz.fix:
Turn it into a transfer question where the commit is the missing piece:
```test predict-setup-files
A friend clones your repo, installs Matt's Skills and types `/to-tickets`. It tells her to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` first, though you ran it weeks ago and chose local markdown. What's the likeliest reason?
- [ ] Setup saved its answers in your plugin's folder, not hers.
  > Setup writes nothing into the plugin. Its answers are plain files in the repo.
- [ ] Setup has to run once per computer, as well as once per repo.
  > It runs once per repo. Its files travel with the repo to every clone.
- [x] You never committed the files setup wrote into the repo.
  > Right. `/to-tickets` finds the tracker through `docs/agents/` and the Agent skills block in `CLAUDE.md`. Uncommitted, those files stayed on your computer.
- [ ] `/to-tickets` is user-invoked, so it can't read setup's files.
  > Being user-invoked limits who can start a Skill, not which files it reads.
```

reader.where: Lost? Ask the router, "Before it describes a Skill or suggests skipping one, it reads that Skill's `SKILL.md`." (line 205), and the router Scene caption "It reads every Skill it's about to recommend or skip" (lines 213-214)

They're there: type the name." Change step 8 (line 316) to: "Read its answer. If it says a Skill isn't installed, ignore that; user-invoked Skills are hidden from it. Then type `/exit`."

reader.where: Who can start a Skill, "(A slash name later in your message only gives the agent permission to run it.)" (line 102), against "Only you can start it... If the agent tries to start one anyway, Claude Code blocks it." (line 100)
reader.problem: This is a contradiction inside the Lesson for a cold reader. Line 100 says only you can start a user-invoked Skill and Claude Code blocks the agent. Two sentences later, a mid-sentence slash name gives the agent "permission to run it". The reader can't tell whether "ok, now /to-spec this" runs the Skill or not. The router-stops feedback then says flatly that it "can't start a user-invoked Skill" (line 234). The docs say the mid-sentence name runs nothing directly; Claude may then run the Skill if your wording asks. The parenthetical gives neither half of that clearly.
reader.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills, "Where you write the skill's name": at the start of the message, Claude Code runs the skill directly. After plain text, nothing runs directly; the name counts as permission and Claude judges from the wording whether to run it. The same page's table says a disable-model-invocation skill can be invoked by Claude "Not on its own", and that if Claude tries anyway, Claude Code blocks the call.
reader.fix: Either cut the parenthetical (saves 14 words; the advice to type it at the start already covers it), or replace it with: "(Later in a sentence, as in "now /to-spec this", the name runs nothing by itself. It only lets the agent start the Skill if your wording asks, so it may not happen. Put it first.)" Then change line 100 to "If the agent tries to start one without your say-so, Claude Code blocks it."

reader.where: Installing Matt's Skills, line 135: "Each answers to its short name, like `/grill-me`, and its full name, `/mattpocock-skills:grill-me`." (also line 97: "You can start any of Matt's Skills by typing `/` and its name.")
reader.problem: The Lesson contradicts itself. Line 135 says every Skill answers to its short name. Lines 239–241 then say the short name `/code-review` reaches Claude Code's review, and that `/prototype` can misbehave too. The table at line 108 lists `/code-review` and `/prototype` as names you can type, so a reader who stops at line 135 will type `/code-review` expecting Matt's review.
reader.evidence: Lesson line 239: "Type the short name and you get Claude Code's." Line 241: "if that short name misbehaves, type `/mattpocock-skills:prototype`". https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills says the bare name "also invokes the skill unless another command already uses that name." .out-of-scope/harness-name-collisions.md:3 lists `/prototype`, `/research` and `/code-review` as names that clash.
reader.fix: Line 135: "Most also answer to their short name, like `/grill-me`; a few share it with Claude Code's own commands (see When a short name is taken). The full name, `/mattpocock-skills:grill-me`, always works."

reader.where: The idea, line 62: "Claude Code notices when you edit a Skill, but if you create a Skills folder that didn't exist when the session started, type `/reload-skills`."
reader.problem: This implies that after one `/reload-skills`, later edits are picked up. The docs say a folder created mid-session isn't watched, so you have to reload again after each change. reader.fix: "... type `/reload-skills`, and again after each later change there until you restart Claude Code."
